solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: “White tie with hot pants” ad redesigned to cover backside (3,3,3,5)

indicatorNotes.redesigned: the letters of the ad are laid out afresh
indicatorNotes.to cover: the rearranged letters sit over and around the next piece

blocks.note: HOT PANTS AD rearranged, ten letters

annotation.surface: A cheeky fashion advert has been redone so that its hot pants now cover the model's bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: White tie is the most formal British dress code: a tailcoat with a white bow tie, traditionally worn with a top hat.
annotation.definitionFit: White tie is the dress code whose outfit is a top hat and tails.

entries.clue: Beasts destroyed gorse (5)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: the word gorse is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

annotation.surface: Some animals have trampled and ruined a patch of gorse bushes.
annotation.walkthrough: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub common on British heaths.
annotation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous brutes, so beasts in the figurative sense.

entries.clue: Harry takes winter vehicle, skipping Germany (6)

indicatorNotes.skipping: SLED leaves out the letter for Germany

blocks.note: has = takes, as in 'has a biscuit'
SLED minus D, the international vehicle code for Germany

annotation.surface: Prince Harry commandeers a sled for a winter trip but gives Germany a miss.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince, but it is the verb: to harry is to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to hassle them with constant demands.

entries.clue: Most eager characters taken in by artist Hirst, I estimate (10)

indicatorNotes.characters taken in by: the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

annotation.surface: Someone guesses at which letters the artist Damien Hirst has absorbed.
annotation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is the British artist of the pickled shark; his name conveniently supplies most of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Thirsty can mean eager, as in thirsty for knowledge, so thirstiest is most eager.

entries.clue: What Islington postcode starts with zero? (4)

blocks.note: surface padding, turning the clue into a question
Islington's postcode is N1: the letter N…

annotation.surface: A quiz question asking which Islington postcode begins with a zero.
annotation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of north London, and its central postcode is N1; read aloud letter by letter it spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nought, the zero quantity, is not any at all.

entries.clue: However casually, hugging friend results in charge! (5-2)

indicatorNotes.hugging: the casual word wraps its arms round the friend

blocks.note: tho' is an informal spelling of though, meaning however

annotation.surface: A sentimental tale: an embrace between friends ends in a criminal charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The charge is not a legal one: tally-ho is the huntsman's cry as the hounds are sent after a fox, used generally as a rallying shout.
annotation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry that sends riders charging after a sighted fox.

entries.clue: Lead-free facilities prepared for bank on paper (9)

indicatorNotes.Lead-free: the word loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.prepared: the remaining letters are made up into a new word

blocks.note: FACILITIES without its first letter F

annotation.surface: Lead-free equipment has been got ready for use at a bank's premises.
annotation.walkthrough: Bank is used as a pilot uses it, to tilt: italic type leans over on the page.
annotation.definitionFit: Italicising text slopes the letters, making them bank as a plane does.

entries.clue: Go out more, avoiding unknown creep when talking tough stuff (9,5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: the phrase drops the unknown Y
indicatorNotes.when talking: the word is to be heard, not read

blocks.note: STAY IN LESS = go out more, minus Y, an algebraic unknown
to steal = to creep, as in steal into a room

annotation.surface: Advice to a shut-in: get out more and stop lurking about speaking tough.
annotation.walkthrough: STAY IN LESS is a roundabout way of saying go out more; dropping the Y takes it to the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Stainless steel is a hard, durable metal alloy: tough stuff.

entries.clue: Disorderly teen’s breaking a raw academic member’s connection (8,6)

indicatorNotes.Disorderly: the letters of teen's are thrown out of order
indicatorNotes.breaking: the jumbled letters burst in between the other pieces

blocks.note: a raw day has a chill
TEENS rearranged, set between A CHILL and DON
a don is a university lecturer

annotation.surface: An unruly teenager has disrupted a young lecturer's link with the university.
annotation.walkthrough: Member here is a limb, the leg; its connection is the tendon joining calf to heel.
annotation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon connects the calf muscle of the leg to the heel bone.

entries.clue: One believes appeal Sir Humphrey’s opening looks retrograde in pen (9)

indicatorNotes.looks retrograde: the three pieces appear running backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the turned-round string goes inside the pen

blocks.note: it = sex appeal, as in the It girl
can = prison (pen); HRISTI goes between C and AN

annotation.surface: A civil servant's charm fades as the TV mandarin Sir Humphrey writes in reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Humphrey is the scheming civil servant of the British TV comedy Yes, Minister. Pen and can are both slang for prison.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a follower of Christ is, above all, someone who holds a faith.

entries.clue: Doe-eyed creature‘s all over relative (5)

blocks.note: taken as it stands, then flipped to LLA

annotation.surface: Someone with big soft eyes is fawned over by the whole family.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is a contraction of is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Llamas are famous for their large, long-lashed eyes.

entries.clue: Piano’s quality’s occasionally lacking, causing aspersions (7)

annotation.surface: A concert review: the piano's tone kept faltering and drew harsh remarks.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophes are ignored; strike alternate letters from PIANOSQUALITYS starting with the P.
annotation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to throw insults at someone.

entries.clue: Scarcity’s hollowed out Iran – I must move from Middle East (6)

indicatorNotes.hollowed out: only the shell of the word is kept
indicatorNotes.must move: the I shifts position within IRAN

blocks.note: IRAN with its I moved one place along

annotation.surface: A news line about shortages in a gutted Iran, whose people must flee the region.
annotation.walkthrough: The I in IRAN only hops one place, from first to second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Syria is in the Middle East, so Syrian means from there.

entries.clue: Planned to feature in Lancet: “Are bile ducts twisted?” (10)

indicatorNotes.to feature in: the answer appears inside the quoted words

blocks.note: lancET ARE BILE Ducts, read from right to left

annotation.surface: A headline from The Lancet medical journal asking whether bile ducts can get kinked.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lancet is a British medical journal, which makes the anatomy look like the point.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something planned was done on purpose, intentionally.

entries.clue: Run out of cannabis with 90 per cent reduction initially (4)

indicatorNotes.with 90 per cent reduction initially: the first letter, read as a Roman numeral, is cut to a tenth

blocks.note: D (500) becomes L (50), a 90 per cent cut

annotation.surface: A dealer has run out of cannabis after prices were slashed at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Run out of looks like one phrase; split it: run is the definition and out of means made from.
annotation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides.

entries.clue: Possible way to get lolly stick more frozen? (3,6)

annotation.surface: An ice-lolly riddle: what makes the stick even colder?
annotation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money, not an ice lolly; NUMBER must be read as numb-er.
annotation.definitionFit: Keying in a PIN number at a cash machine is one way to withdraw money.

entries.clue: Work regime that could mean four being cut (4-2-4)

blocks.note: a drop of four, as when one number is lowered to a smaller one

annotation.surface: A job that could involve four staff being laid off.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is arithmetic: nine down to five is a cut of four.
annotation.definitionFit: Nine-to-five describes the usual office working day.

entries.clue: No safety net and no rubber ring? (4,2,4)

annotation.definition: No safety net and no rubber ring?

blocks.note: the figurative reading: nothing to catch you if you fail
the literal reading: someone dropped in water with no float

annotation.surface: A swimmer, or a trapeze artist, facing the water with nothing to catch them.
annotation.walkthrough: Taken literally, a non-swimmer without a rubber ring must sink or swim; figuratively, no safety net means succeeding or failing unaided.
annotation.definitionFit: Sink or swim describes a situation where you succeed or fail with no help.

entries.clue: Old saint substantially funded this African native’s fast (7)

annotation.surface: A wealthy old saint bankrolled an African native's fast.
annotation.walkthrough: Fast looks like going without food, but it is speed: the ostrich is the fastest bird on land.
annotation.definitionFit: The ostrich is native to Africa, and famously fast.

entries.clue: Margaret briefly flipped about son’s sparklers (4)

blocks.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret

annotation.surface: Margaret briefly lost her temper over her son's fireworks.
annotation.walkthrough: Sparklers look like the hand-held fireworks, but here they are jewels.
annotation.definitionFit: Gems sparkle, so sparklers is a playful word for jewels.

entries.clue: Man with self at heart in place of religion (6)

indicatorNotes.at heart: only the core of the word is taken

blocks.note: the middle two letters of sELf

annotation.surface: A man with his inner self at peace in a house of worship.
annotation.walkthrough: With looks like a link but joins the two pieces in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship.

entries.clue: Back street with neat vents (6)

indicatorNotes.Back: everything after it is read backwards

annotation.surface: A back street lined with tidy air vents.
annotation.walkthrough: Vents is a verb here, as a volcano vents; neat is used as of a spirit, unmixed.
annotation.definitionFit: A volcano that vents erupts, releasing lava and gas.

entries.clue: Good day to cut former part in show (7)

indicatorNotes.to cut: the greeting slices into the other pieces

blocks.note: a greeting, placed between EX and BIT

annotation.surface: An actor has a good day as a former role is trimmed from the show.
annotation.walkthrough: Good day is a greeting, like hi, not a verdict on the day.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put paintings on public display in a gallery.

entries.clue: Set about panhandler, half knocked down, not out (5)

indicatorNotes.half knocked down: half the word is struck off

blocks.note: in = not out, as a batter still in

annotation.surface: A beggar is beaten half senseless and left not quite out cold.
annotation.walkthrough: A panhandler is a beggar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: set about a task means make a start on it.

entries.clue: Sting starts on Stewart Copeland, Andy mediates (4)

indicatorNotes.starts on: take the first letter of each following word

annotation.surface: Sting and Stewart Copeland fall out and Andy Summers steps in to make peace.
annotation.walkthrough: Sting, Stewart Copeland and Andy Summers were the three members of The Police, but Sting here is a con.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: a sting is an elaborate confidence trick or swindle.

entries.clue: Where many Arabic speakers are audible, ignoring the French rambling (5)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: the French article is left out
indicatorNotes.rambling: the leftover letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: AUDIBLE minus LE, French for the

annotation.surface: Arabic speakers can be heard talking aimlessly, dropping their French.
annotation.walkthrough: Audible looks like a sound instruction but is simply the word to be taken apart.
annotation.definitionFit: Dubai is an Arabic-speaking emirate of the UAE.

entries.clue: Feigned tenderness in speech toasted with this? (9)

indicatorNotes.in speech: the words are to be heard, not read

annotation.surface: A wedding speech full of false affection, followed by the toast.
annotation.walkthrough: Tenderness is soreness here, not affection: pain.
annotation.definitionFit: Champagne is the usual drink for a toast.

entries.clue: No right digit found by emergency room – left also seeking location (14)

annotation.surface: A patient missing a finger heads for the ER, but gets lost on the way.
annotation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county, on the Scottish border.
annotation.definitionFit: Northumberland is a place, a county of north-east England.
